items.claim: The regnal accession, evaluation, and rebellion notice at Jer.52.1-3 form one dated backstory unit correctly closed before the fresh onset at Jer.52.4, with its quotes, ketiv/qere, and paseq disclosures all byte-accurate.
items.evidence: Both witnesses' quoted text match the staged verse text exactly at Jer.52.1-3; the ketiv/qere at Jer.52.1 and the paseq at Jer.52.3 both match the disclosure inventories and carry proper single-witness, count-only framing. The undisclosed setumah standing at the immediately preceding verse, Jer.51.64, is weak tier-3 corroboration only and does not drive this boundary, which the colophon content at that verse and the appendix onset at Jer.52.1 already secure independently; its non-citation here is not a substantive gap.
tier_citations: parashah disclosure inventory, oshb:Jer.51.64 (SAMEKH, tier-3 weak)

items.claim: The dated siege-to-imprisonment chain at Jer.52.4-11 is correctly held as one unit with no intervening tier-1 seam, and its quotes and ketiv/qere disclosure are byte-accurate.
items.evidence: Both witnesses' quoted text match the staged verse text exactly at Jer.52.4, 52.5, 52.9, and 52.11; the ketiv/qere at Jer.52.11 matches the disclosure inventory. Jer.52.5's until-the-eleventh-year notice uses a terminus construction rather than the book's verse-initial dated-onset shape, so reading it as continuing the siege opened at Jer.52.4 rather than as a fresh onset is byte-grounded, and no koh-amar, word-event, or further date formula intervenes before the capture and sentencing that close the span.

items.claim: The unit's closing seam at Jer.52.16/17 rests on a bare change of narrated object rather than a disclosed tier-1 device, and an in-span paseq goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: The opening at Jer.52.12 is well-grounded (a month-first dated notice paired with a newly entering named agent), but no koh-amar, word-event formula, or fresh date notice separates Jer.52.16 from Jer.52.17; the captain of the guard commissioned at Jer.52.12 remains the continuous acting authority across that seam, so the strongest rejected alternative should have weighed holding the destruction, deportation, and temple-vessel reports together as one dated unit rather than splitting them on subject matter alone, making the high-confidence rating optimistic for this boundary. Separately, a paseq stands at Jer.52.15 (single-witness WLC, seg layer, count-only) inside this span and is not disclosed.

items.claim: Both boundaries of this unit rest on a bare change of narrated object rather than a disclosed tier-1 device, and an in-span paseq goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: Jer.52.16/17 and Jer.52.23/24 both cut on subject matter alone (the temple's bronze against the population notice before it and the named officials after it), with no koh-amar, word-event formula, date onset, or newly entering participant disclosed at either seam; the device notes' own admission that the shift from the collective Chaldeans at Jer.52.17 to the captain of the guard at Jer.52.19 as acting agent is left unresolved inside the unit undercuts treating the equally deviceless outer seams as boundary-worthy, making the high-confidence rating optimistic. A paseq stands at Jer.52.20 (single-witness WLC, seg layer, count-only) and is not disclosed.

items.claim: The unit's opening seam at Jer.52.23/24 rests on a bare change of narrated object rather than a disclosed tier-1 device.
items.evidence: No koh-amar, word-event formula, or fresh date notice marks Jer.52.24, and the captain of the guard remains the continuous commissioning agent from the dated onset at Jer.52.12 through the officials' seizure; treating this shift in the narrated object as an addressee or participant shift overstates what the bytes carry, since no new agent enters and no one is newly addressed here. The strongest rejected alternative should have weighed holding the temple-inventory and officials-seizure reports together as one dated unit rather than splitting them on subject matter alone, making the high-confidence rating optimistic for this boundary; the closing seam at Jer.52.27/28 is by contrast well-grounded on the fresh dated, self-referential chronicle that follows.

items.claim: The three-entry deportation chronicle at Jer.52.28-30 is correctly held as one accounting under its shared governing clause, with quotes and the closing petuchah disclosure byte-accurate and its close-call framing appropriately hedged.
items.evidence: Both witnesses' quoted text match the staged verse text exactly at Jer.52.28 and 52.30; the petuchah at Jer.52.30 matches the disclosure inventory and is correctly framed as tier-3 weak corroboration, not a driver. The rejected alternative of three independent one-entry spans is the genuine strongest rival here and is honestly engaged rather than strawmanned, and the medium-confidence, frontier-flagged rating matches the real closeness of the call.
tier_citations: parashah disclosure inventory, oshb:Jer.52.30 (PE, tier-3 weak)

items.claim: The Jehoiachin-release notice at Jer.52.31-34 is correctly opened on its own dated, scene-shifted onset and closed at the chapter's own end, with quotes and both ketiv/qere pairs byte-accurate.
items.evidence: Both witnesses' quoted text match the staged verse text exactly at Jer.52.31 and 52.34; the ketiv/qere pairs at Jer.52.31 (the confinement word) and Jer.52.32 (the other kings) both match the disclosure inventory with accurate consonantal-versus-received readings. The dating clause at Jer.52.31 opens the unit on a fresh chronology tied to a different king's accession, satisfying both the date-onset and participant-shift grounds for a boundary, and the two spellings of Jehoiachin's name within that verse are correctly read as one name-form's byform variation rather than a distinct name-form.
